_readme: Committed baseline of pre-existing gosec HIGH findings (issue #532).
The gate in .github/scripts/gosec-gate.sh fails CI on any HIGH finding that is
NOT covered here. It never lowers gosec's own severity threshold: gosec runs
unfiltered over ./... and every finding is reported; this file only records the
HIGH findings that were present when the gate was introduced, each with a
reason. MEDIUM and LOW are counted and printed, not gated (issue #532
Match key is (rule, file, count). Line numbers and code snippets are
deliberately NOT part of the key: gosec's snippet spans neighbouring lines, so
a snippet-keyed baseline would red-fail on edits that have nothing to do with
the finding, and a scanner that fails every PR gets switched off. Known gap of
the count key: swapping one finding of a rule for a different finding of the
same rule in the same file stays suppressed. Accepted deliberately.
To accept a new HIGH: add an entry with a real reason, or prefer an inline
#nosec in the source, which is narrower. To retire one: drop the entry (the
gate warns, it does not fail, when actual < allowed).
status: 'accepted' = read, verdict written below. 'deferred' = NOT yet read;
the gate holds the line at today's count while triage happens. Do not relabel
a deferred entry to accepted without writing the verdict.

entries.reason: Constant is the NAME of an environment variable (SKYSCANNER_API_KEY), not a key. The secret itself is read from the environment at runtime.
SourceFeeds is a map of public RSS feed URLs. G101 pattern-matches the word 'secret' in a source key, not a credential.
Public Overpass API endpoint URL. No authentication of any kind is involved.
Two long English warning strings shown to the user about round-trip pricing. High-entropy prose, not a credential.
Public subscription key that matka.fi ships to every visitor in its JS bundle. Not a private credential; rotating it would break parity with the public site.
Public API key embedded in the Finnlines booking SPA bundle and served to every visitor. Not a private credential.
Public API key embedded in the NS website JS and served to every visitor. Not a private credential.
Public Priority Pass search endpoint URL, overridable in tests. No credential.
Cookie NAME constant ('aws-waf-token'). The value is issued by the remote WAF at runtime and never appears in source.
int -> rune on '0' + single decimal digit. The digit is produced by dividing by a power of ten, so the range is 0-9 by construction.
int -> byte in fixed-width numeric padding helpers, where each operand is already reduced by /1000, /10 or %10 to a single digit.
int64 -> byte after an explicit 8-bit shift-and-mask in a byte-packing loop; truncation is the intended operation.

Deliberate detached background refresh: the goroutine outlives the request that triggered it, so inheriting the request context would cancel the refresh on response. It builds its own context with a timeout.
math/rand is used only for retry backoff jitter. Jitter is a thundering-herd mitigation, not a security control, and needs no CSPRNG.

ACCEPTED RISK (V). runPrefsEdit builds exec.Command(editor, path) with no shell: argv is exactly two elements, so $EDITOR cannot smuggle arguments (a value like 'vim -c ...' is looked up as one binary name and fails). editor resolves $EDITOR -> $VISUAL -> 'vi' at cmd/trvl/prefs.go:216-222; path is os.UserHomeDir()+/.trvl/preferences.json at :201-205, never user-supplied. The residual risk is an attacker who already controls the operator's environment, who by then already has code execution as that user. CLI-only path, not reachable from the MCP server.

NOT REACHABLE (V). The tainted value is cfgPath, and the sink at cmd/trvl/mcp_install.go:277 writes cfgPath+".trvl.bak". cfgPath comes only from clientConfigPath (:66-109), a closed switch over literal home-relative paths; this particular sink sits behind the isCodexTOML/'codex' branch, and any unrecognised client returns an error at :109 instead of a path. No caller-supplied string ever reaches the write, so the backup can only land next to a known config file.

MITIGATED (V, trvl#539 TRVL.HARDEN.3). The sink is the preferences BACKUP write, dst = prefsPathIn(dir)+".bak."+suffix. dir is ~/.trvl. The version component was previously unvalidated: it comes from ReadStamp, i.e. the trimmed contents of a file on disk, NOT from the compiled-in Version, so a corrupted or externally-written stamp chose part of the path. backupPreferences now refuses any stamp failing safeVersionStamp (allowlist of [0-9A-Za-z._+-], no "..", non-empty, <=64 chars) and backs up under a GENERATED suffix instead -- "unknown-" plus the process clock, so no caller-supplied string reaches the path AND the safety net survives an unreadable stamp. Refusing the stamp by skipping the backup was the earlier attempt and was rejected in review: it deleted the user's only pre-migration copy in exactly the state most likely to need it. Pinned by TestBackupPreferencesRefusesUnsafeVersionStamp, which asserts both no-escape and backup-still-exists, with a control that a valid stamp still names its own backup; sabotage-verified by removing the guard.

NOT REACHABLE (V), both findings. internal/destinations/attractions.go:72-73 builds the URL with fmt.Sprintf from a base plus %d and two %.6f and the API key: GetAttractions takes lat/lon as float64 and radius as int (:50), so no string from a caller can reach the host or path. The base is openTripMapAPIURL (:18-20), a package var initialised from a literal const and overridden only in tests, and the key comes from os.Getenv(OPENTRIPMAP_API_KEY) (:51) and is appended last in the query. Hardening note, RESOLVED 2026-08-06 (#539): internal/destinations/http.go used to build a plain http.Client with no dial guard, so a compromised upstream could steer a request at a private address. It now routes through providers.GuardedTransport(), which carries the destination policy on its dialer and is returned as an opaque http.RoundTripper so a consumer cannot replace that dialer. Kept as a note rather than deleted: this entry accepts the finding on the URL-construction argument alone, and that argument stands on its own.

NOT REACHABLE (V), both findings. doSearchRequest (internal/providers/auth.go:382-407) replays orig.URL of a request that was already built and already sent; the URL originates from substituteVars(cfg.Endpoint, vars) in internal/providers/runtime_provider.go:208. What holds unconditionally is the dial-time guard: guardedDialer/guardedTransport installs dialControl on every provider client (internal/providers/destination.go:137-181, wired in runtime_core.go), and dialControl refuses the connection on the RESOLVED IP - loopback, private, link-local, unspecified and multicast (refusedIP :57-79) - so a redirected or substituted host cannot reach an internal address regardless of how the string was built. The parse-time providers.CheckDestinationURL on Endpoint and Auth.PreflightURL (mcp/tools_providers.go, destination.go:90-125) is a secondary check only: substituteVars is a raw strings.ReplaceAll with no escaping (internal/providers/mapping.go:12-18) and runs after it. Scheme and host are literal in the shipped templates (I, checked by search, not enforced by code). Sole opt-out is the operator-set env var TRVL_ALLOW_LOCAL_PROVIDERS (destination.go:27, :41-48).

NOT REACHABLE, AND NOW ENFORCED (V, trvl#539 TRVL.HARDEN.2). The sink is testRedirectTransport.RoundTrip, which rewrites every request to a baseURL settable only by NewTestClient. This entry previously lived on internal/batchexec/client.go and rested on an observation -- 'the only callers are *_test.go files' -- which was true when written and which nothing checked. A future production caller would have made this finding live WITHOUT changing the baseline count, so the gate would have stayed green. The helper now lives in its own file with no production code in it, and scripts/ci/check-test-only-helpers.sh fails if any non-test file references it (sabotage-verified, exits 1). Moving it into a _test.go file would have been stronger still -- a production caller would fail to compile -- but _test.go is built only when testing its own package, and 12 files across internal/flights, internal/hotels and internal/explore need this helper. The issue named the lint rule as the fallback for exactly that case.
